questions.question_text: The reciprocal of a number is $2\frac{1}{2}$. What is the number?

options.why: Converted $2\frac{1}{2}$ to the improper fraction $\frac{5}{2}$ but stopped there without swapping.
Gave the opposite of $2\frac{1}{2}$ instead of reversing the reciprocal.
Reciprocated only the whole-number part $2$ and dropped the fraction part.

questions.solution_text:
$2\frac{1}{2}=\frac{5}{2}$
Swapping numerator and denominator is its own reverse.
The number is $\frac{2}{5}$.
Check: $\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{5}{2}=1$.

questions.question_text: Which of these numbers is equal to its own reciprocal?

options.why: Its reciprocal is $\frac{1}{2}$, which is not equal to $2$.
Its reciprocal is $2$, which is not equal to $\frac{1}{2}$.
Zero has no reciprocal, because you cannot divide by $0$.

questions.solution_text:
A number equals its own reciprocal when $n=\frac{1}{n}$.
$n^{2}=1$
$n=1$
